slides.texte_overlay:
How to handle a rude comment
with class

Pause before you react. Two seconds of silence, a calm face. Most rude comments are fishing for a reaction. When you don't give one right away, the other person suddenly looks a lot less sure of themselves.
Ask a simple question back. "What do you mean by that?" Said calmly, not angrily. People who throw cheap shots rarely want to explain them out loud, and they usually back down on their own.
Agree with the fair part, ignore the rest. "You're right, I was late. I'll fix it." Taking the true bit seriously takes away all the drama, and the rude part has nothing left to stand on.
Keep a calm, steady mind. Five minutes a day of history, art or science reminds you how small most drama is. People who know a lot about the world rarely get rattled by one rude guy.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It reminds me how small most drama is. Hard to get rattled by one rude guy after that.

slides.texte_overlay: Use their name and stay polite. "Mark, I'd rather we keep this respectful." Calm and direct, no insult back. In front of other people, the one who stays polite always wins the room.
Don't explain yourself to someone who isn't listening. One sentence, then stop. "I see it differently." You don't owe a long defense to someone who just wants to argue.
Know when to walk away. "I'm going to grab a drink." Leaving a pointless argument isn't losing. It's choosing where your energy goes, and that's the classiest move of all.
